Freeport Reports
Third-Quarter and Nine-Month 2026 Results
•Third-quarter 2026 consolidated copper and gold production in line with expectations
◦Copper sales volumes approximated prior estimates
◦Gold sales volumes impacted by previously reported timing of gold sales in Indonesia
•Ramp-up of mining operations in the Grasberg minerals district met expectations with significant growth expected in 2027 and 2028
•Operations at PTFI’s smelter re-commenced in late August 2026
•Advancing organic copper growth projects, including:
◦Opportunities for scaling innovative leach and technology initiatives in the Americas and potential significant brownfield expansions in the U.S.
◦Potential major expansion at El Abra in Chile
•Strong margins and cash flow generation; positive future outlook
•Net income attributable to common stock in third-quarter 2026 totaled $1.2 billion, $0.81 per share, and adjusted net income attributable to common stock totaled $1.3 billion, $0.88 per share.
•Consolidated production totaled 832 million pounds of copper, 234 thousand ounces of gold and 22 million pounds of molybdenum in third-quarter 2026.
•Consolidated sales totaled 749 million pounds of copper, 105 thousand ounces of gold and 22 million pounds of molybdenum in third-quarter 2026.
•Consolidated sales are expected to approximate 3.0 billion pounds of copper, 649 thousand ounces of gold and 93 million pounds of molybdenum for the year 2026, including 875 million pounds of copper, 300 thousand ounces of gold and 22 million pounds of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026.
•Average realized prices were $6.54 per pound for copper, $4,273 per ounce for gold and $32.46 per pound for molybdenum in third-quarter 2026.
•Average unit net cash costs were $2.07 per pound of copper in third-quarter 2026 and are expected to average $1.90 per pound of copper for the year 2026.
•Operating cash flows totaled $2.0 billion, net of $0.4 billion of working capital and other uses, in third-quarter 2026. Assuming prices of $6.50 per pound for copper, $4,000 per ounce for gold and $32.00 per pound for molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026, operating cash flows are expected to approximate $8.5 billion, net of $0.6 billion of working capital and other uses, for the year 2026.
•Capital expenditures totaled $1.2 billion, including $0.7 billion for major mining projects, in third-quarter 2026. Capital expenditures are expected to approximate $4.4 billion, including $3.0 billion for major mining projects, for the year 2026.
•At September 30, 2026, consolidated debt totaled $9.4 billion and consolidated cash and cash equivalents totaled $4.3 billion. At September 30, 2026, net debt totaled $1.8 billion, excluding $3.2 billion of debt for PT Freeport Indonesia’s (PTFI) downstream processing facilities. Refer to the supplemental schedule, “Net Debt,” on page IX.
•During third-quarter 2026, FCX purchased 1.4 million shares of its common stock for a total cost of $102 million ($70.75 average cost per share), bringing share purchases for the first nine months of 2026 to 4.9 million shares for $305 million ($62.69 average cost per share).

1
PHOENIX, AZ, October 27, 2026 – Freeport (NYSE: FCX) reported third-quarter 2026 net income attributable to common stock of $1.2 billion, $0.81 per share, and adjusted net income attributable to common stock of $1.3 billion, $0.88 per share, after excluding after-tax net charges totaling $101 million, $0.07 per share, primarily for idle facility and restoration costs associated with PTFI’s September 2025 external mud rush incident. For additional information, refer to the supplemental schedule, “Adjusted Net Income,” beginning on page VII.

Kathleen Quirk, President and Chief Executive Officer, said, “The Freeport team delivered strong financial results in the third quarter and achieved several important milestones to drive value and support future growth. We made continued steady progress with our Grasberg ramp-up and advanced innovative leach and technology initiatives in our Americas business to enhance performance and growth options. Favorable pricing for our products, particularly for copper and molybdenum, drove strong margins with substantial conversion to bottom-line results, highlighting the strength of our diversified portfolio. We remain focused on operational excellence, delivering growing volumes at Grasberg safely and sustainably and expanding production from our existing asset base to increase margins, cash flow and earnings. Freeport is strongly positioned as America’s Copper Champion® and as a global copper leader with large-scale, geographically diverse operations and a pipeline of attractive growth options to support a growing market and build value for stakeholders.”

Consolidated Production and Sales Volumes
Copper
•Third-quarter 2026 production of 832 million pounds was in line with expectations, with slightly better results from Indonesia and South America operations offsetting lower production in the U.S. Third-quarter 2026 production exceeded sales by approximately 11%, primarily reflecting in-process inventories at smelting operations in Indonesia. Third-quarter 2026 sales of 749 million pounds were in line with the July 2026 estimate of 750 million pounds.
•As expected, third-quarter 2026 sales were below third-quarter 2025 sales of 1.0 billion pounds, primarily reflecting lower operating rates at PTFI during the ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine and timing of shipments.
Gold
•Third-quarter 2026 production of 234 thousand ounces was in line with expectations. Third-quarter 2026 sales of 105 thousand ounces were significantly below third-quarter 2026 production primarily resulting from in-process inventories at smelting and refining operations and timing of sales. Third-quarter 2026 gold sales were lower than the July 2026 estimate of 160 thousand ounces, primarily reflecting the timing of refined gold sales in Indonesia.
•Third-quarter 2026 sales were below third-quarter 2025 sales, reflecting the timing of sales and lower operating rates at PTFI during the ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine.
Molybdenum
•Third-quarter 2026 sales of 22 million pounds were in line with the July 2026 estimate and higher than third-quarter 2025 sales of 19 million pounds, primarily reflecting timing of shipments.
Consolidated sales volumes for the year 2026 are expected to approximate 3.0 billion pounds of copper, 649 thousand ounces of gold and 93 million pounds of molybdenum, including 875 million pounds of copper, 300 thousand ounces of gold and 22 million pounds of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026. With the projected significant increase in gold sales in fourth-quarter 2026, PTFI may sell gold in the export market to the extent not required by

3
the domestic market. PTFI is seeking clarity from the Indonesia government on administrative procedures for PTFI’s refined gold exports since current regulations (specifying a 10% export duty) conflict with the terms in PTFI’s special mining business license (IUPK) (which do not require the payment of duties on refined gold exports).
Consolidated copper and gold production volumes for the year 2026 are expected to exceed sales volumes, reflecting deferrals of approximately 100 million pounds of copper and 70 thousand ounces of gold associated with inventory held at PTFI’s smelting operations.
Consolidated Unit Net Cash Costs
Consolidated unit net cash costs (net of by-product credits and excluding idle facility, direct recovery and restoration costs associated with the ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine) for FCX’s copper mines averaged $2.07 per pound of copper in third-quarter 2026, which was 4% above the July 2026 estimate of $2.00 per pound, primarily reflecting lower by-product credits as a result of the deferral of gold sales from third-quarter 2026 to fourth-quarter 2026.
Third-quarter 2026 average unit net cash costs were higher than third-quarter 2025 average unit net cash costs of $1.40 per pound of copper, primarily reflecting the impact of lower copper and gold volumes at PTFI and higher production costs, including for energy and other consumables.
During the ramp-up period of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine and until PTFI’s operations return to normal capacity, a portion of PTFI's production and delivery costs will be recognized as idle facility costs, which are non-inventoriable. Idle facility, direct recovery and restoration costs totaled $244 million in third-quarter 2026, $934 million for the first nine months of 2026 and $171 million in both third-quarter 2025 and for the first nine months of 2025, which were excluded from consolidated net cash costs.
Based on achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates and assuming average prices of $4,000 per ounce of gold and $32.00 per pound of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026, consolidated unit net cash costs (net of by-product credits and excluding idle facility and restoration costs) for FCX’s copper mines are expected to average $1.90 per pound of copper for the year 2026 (including $1.68 per pound of copper in fourth-quarter 2026).
The impact of price changes on consolidated unit net cash costs for the year 2026 would approximate $0.01 per pound of copper for each $100 per ounce change in the average price of gold during fourth-quarter 2026 and $0.01 per pound of copper for each $2 per pound change in the average price of molybdenum during fourth-quarter 2026.
Projected sales volumes and unit net cash costs for the year 2026 are dependent on operational performance; the ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine and smelter at PTFI; impacts related to the conflict in the Middle East, including changes in energy costs and other consumables; weather-related conditions; timing of shipments and sales and other factors detailed in the “Cautionary Statement” below.
OPERATIONS
Leaching and Technology Innovation Initiatives. FCX is incorporating new applications, technologies and data analytics into its leaching processes across its United States (U.S.) and South America operations to strengthen long-term cost competitiveness and unlock significant value. Incremental copper production from these initiatives totaled 55 million pounds in third-quarter 2026 and 156 million pounds for the first nine months of 2026.
FCX is targeting an increase in production from these initiatives from the current run rate of approximately 220 million pounds of copper per annum to 300 million pounds in 2027, with potential for further significant increases in recoverable metal in future years. FCX continues to deploy large-scale testing of an internally developed additive at its Morenci operations, where early results have been encouraging. In addition, FCX has developed two customized additives that are being manufactured and are expected to be deployed at multiple stockpiles in the first half of 2027. Laboratory testing of these newly developed additives has demonstrated significant improvements in copper recoveries. FCX is also advancing projects to use heat sources to increase the temperature of its stockpiles to boost copper recoveries. Success with these initiatives has the potential to contribute to additions in recoverable copper in leach stockpiles and favorably impact average unit net cash costs.
In addition to its innovative leaching initiatives, FCX is pursuing opportunities to leverage new technologies and analytic tools in automation and operating practices with a goal of improving operating efficiencies and reducing costs and capital intensity of its current operations and future development projects. FCX believes its innovative leaching and technology initiatives will strengthen its operational performance and enhance opportunities for profitable growth.

4
United States. FCX manages seven copper operations in the U.S. – Morenci, Bagdad, Safford (including Lone Star), Sierrita and Miami in Arizona, and Chino and Tyrone in New Mexico. FCX also operates a copper smelter and rod mill in Miami, Arizona, and a copper refinery and rod mill in El Paso, Texas. In addition to copper, certain of these operations produce molybdenum concentrate, gold and silver.
All of FCX’s U.S. operations are wholly owned, except for Morenci. FCX records its 72% undivided joint venture interest in Morenci using the proportionate consolidation method.
Development Activities. FCX has substantial reserves, resources and future opportunities for organic growth in the U.S. associated with existing operations. Several initiatives are underway to target significant future growth in U.S. copper operations, including the leaching and technology innovation initiatives discussed above.
FCX has conducted technical and economic studies to more than double the concentrator capacity of the Bagdad operation in northwest Arizona. Bagdad’s reserve life currently exceeds 80 years and supports an expanded operation. FCX expects to reach an investment decision on the expansion project in fourth-quarter 2026. The studies indicate the opportunity to construct new concentrating facilities to increase copper production by 200 to 250 million pounds per year and increase molybdenum production by 10 to 12 million pounds per year. Expanded operations would position Bagdad as the second-largest copper mine in the U.S. (behind FCX’s flagship Morenci mine) and among the lowest cost mines in FCX’s U.S. portfolio, and Bagdad would benefit from economies of scale, modernized operating models, improved efficiency and lower long-term unit net cash costs.
Capital cost estimates for the Bagdad expansion are being finalized, taking into account current estimates, including for materials, equipment and labor. Current estimates, which remain under review, indicate future incremental capital costs for a new concentrator, mining equipment and expanded infrastructure to approximate $4.5 billion. The project economics are supported at an incentive copper price of approximately $4.00 per pound and would require three to four years to complete. The decision to proceed with and timing of the potential expansion will take into account overall copper market conditions and other factors.
FCX is advancing pre-feasibility studies in the Safford/Lone Star district to define a potential significant expansion opportunity. Positive drilling conducted in recent years indicates a large, mineralized district with opportunities to pursue a large expansion project. FCX expects to complete initial studies in 2027. The decision to proceed with and timing of the potential expansion will take into account results of technical and economic studies, overall copper market conditions and other factors.

FCX’s consolidated copper sales volumes from its U.S. copper mines of 333 million pounds in third-quarter 2026 were slightly lower than third-quarter 2025 copper sales volumes of 339 million pounds. Consolidated copper sales from FCX’s U.S. copper mines are expected to approximate 1.3 billion pounds for the year 2026.
FCX’s U.S. copper mines faced challenging operating conditions in third-quarter 2026 associated with an increased frequency of extreme weather conditions, which adversely affected operating rates and productivity. Although third-quarter 2026 operating rates at FCX’s U.S. copper mines were 10% higher than those in third-quarter 2025, they were approximately 3% to 5% below expectations and operating rates achieved in second-quarter 2026.
Average unit net cash costs (net of by-product credits) for the U.S. copper mines of $3.16 per pound of copper in third-quarter 2026 were higher than third-quarter 2025 average unit net cash costs of $3.11 per pound of copper. Unit costs in third-quarter 2026 were adversely impacted by lower volumes from reduced productivity and higher costs for energy and other inputs, partially offset by higher by-product credits.
Based on achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates and assuming an average price of $32.00 per pound of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026, average unit net cash costs (net of by-product credits) for the U.S. copper mines are expected to approximate $3.08 per pound of copper for the year 2026. The U.S. copper mines’ average unit net cash costs for the year 2026 would change by approximately $0.01 per pound for each $2 per pound change in the average price of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026.
South America. FCX manages two copper operations in South America – Cerro Verde in Peru (55.66%-owned) and El Abra in Chile (51%-owned). These operations are consolidated in FCX’s financial statements. In addition to copper, the Cerro Verde mine produces molybdenum concentrate and silver.
Development Activities. At the El Abra operations in Chile, FCX is advancing the permitting process for a significant expansion opportunity to include a major mill facility similar to the large-scale concentrator at Cerro Verde. The project could result in the addition of over 700 million pounds of copper production per year. In March 2026, El Abra submitted an environmental impact study to Chile regulatory authorities and continues to advance the regulatory process. Preliminary estimates, which remain under review, indicate project capital costs of approximately $7.5 billion (based on estimates prepared in 2024) with project economics supported using an incentive copper price of less than $4.00 per pound. The decision to proceed with and timing of the potential project will take into account required permitting, market conditions and other factors.

FCX’s consolidated copper sales volumes from South America operations of 263 million pounds in third-quarter 2026 were lower than third-quarter 2025 copper sales volumes of 278 million pounds, primarily reflecting slightly lower production resulting from lower ore grades and the timing of shipments. Copper sales from South America operations are expected to approximate 1.0 billion pounds for the year 2026.
Average unit net cash costs (net of by-product credits) for South America operations were $2.39 per pound of copper in third-quarter 2026 compared to average unit net cash costs of $2.30 per pound of copper in third-quarter 2025. In addition to the impact of lower volumes, unit net cash costs were impacted by higher costs for employee profit sharing at Cerro Verde, energy and other inputs, and maintenance and contractor costs at El Abra, partially offset by higher by-product credits.
Based on achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates and assuming an average price of $32.00 per pound of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026, average unit net cash costs (net of by-product credits) for South America operations are expected to approximate $2.59 per pound of copper for the year 2026. South America operations’ average unit net cash costs for the year 2026 would change by approximately $0.02 per pound for each $2 per pound change in the average price of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026.

Indonesia. PTFI operates one of the world’s largest copper and gold mines at the Grasberg minerals district in Central Papua, Indonesia. In addition to copper and gold, the Grasberg minerals district also produces silver. With the completion of its downstream processing facilities, PTFI is a fully integrated producer of refined copper, gold and silver. FCX has a 48.76% ownership interest in PTFI and manages its operations. PTFI’s results are consolidated in FCX’s financial statements.
Operating, Development and Exploration Activities. Over a multi-year investment period, PTFI has successfully commissioned three large-scale underground mines in the Grasberg minerals district (Grasberg Block Cave, Deep Mill Level Zone (DMLZ) and Big Gossan) and completed related expansion of the milling facilities. At normal operating rates, PTFI’s underground operations produce approximately 1.7 billion pounds of copper and 1.3 million ounces of gold per year and are among the lowest-cost copper mining operations in the world.
PTFI has identified additional exploration targets to leverage its infrastructure in the Grasberg minerals district, including a potential extension below the DMLZ underground mine, which requires further drilling and evaluation.
Kucing Liar. Since 2022, PTFI has conducted long-term mine development activities at its Kucing Liar deposit in the Grasberg minerals district. PTFI’s long-term mine plans include a ramp-up of Kucing Liar, commencing in the 2030 timeframe, to a design capacity of approximately 130,000 metric tons of ore per day. The project start-up schedule is under review. Average annual production from Kucing Liar at full operating rates would approximate 750 million pounds of copper and 735 thousand ounces of gold and would enable continuity of large-scale production in the Grasberg minerals district.
As of September 30, 2026, PTFI has incurred approximately $1.6 billion for Kucing Liar development, and capital investments are estimated to approximate an additional $4 billion through 2033 (averaging approximately $0.5 billion per year).
Long-Term Mining Rights. In February 2026, FCX and PTFI entered into a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with the Indonesia government for a life of resource extension of operating rights in the Grasberg minerals district beyond the current expiration in 2041. Under the terms of the MOU, FCX would maintain its current ownership interest in PTFI of 48.76% through 2041 and hold approximately 37% beginning in 2042. The existing governance and operating structure, and terms of the existing shareholder agreement, IUPK and other agreements in effect will continue over the life of the resource.
An extension would enable continuity of large-scale operations for the benefit of all stakeholders and provide growth options through additional resource development opportunities in the highly attractive Grasberg minerals district.
In June 2026, PTFI submitted its application for extension of its IUPK, and FCX and PTFI are working with the Indonesia government to complete the formal license process. The extension of operating rights and other terms are subject to, among other things, the Indonesia government’s issuance of an amended IUPK.


7
Grasberg Block Cave Ramp-Up. Following the September 2025 external mud rush incident, PTFI has made significant progress with the ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine to achieve a safe and sustainable ramp-up to full operating capacity.
In third-quarter 2026, mill throughput averaged 141 thousand metric tons of ore per day (67% of capacity), including 70 thousand metric tons of ore per day from the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine. PTFI continues to expect to reach 80% of capacity in mid-2027 and approach full capacity by year-end 2027.
PTFI completed remediation and restoration activities required for the restart of Production Blocks 2 and 3 and commenced initial ramp-up activities at the end of March 2026. Upgrades to the material handling system at the Grasberg Block Cave haulage level have progressed on schedule with expected completion by early 2027. Preparations continue for the targeted restart of production from Production Block 1S by mid-2027.
Downstream Processing Facilities. PTFI’s smelter and PT Smelting, PTFI’s 66%-owned smelter and refinery in Gresik, Indonesia, smelt and refine copper concentrate from PTFI, and the Precious Metals Refinery (PMR) processes anode slimes from PTFI’s smelter and PT Smelting.
PTFI has combined smelting capacity, including PT Smelting, to produce up to approximately 800,000 metric tons of cathode annually, and the PMR is capable of processing all of PTFI’s gold production.
Following the September 2025 external mud rush incident, during the ramp-up period of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine, smelting operations in Indonesia at both PTFI’s smelter and PT Smelting were adjusted as a result of limited copper concentrate availability. PT Smelting resumed operations in late 2025 and PTFI’s smelter successfully re-commenced operations in late August 2026. Ramp-up activities are proceeding in line with expectations.
FCX expects higher variability between PTFI’s production and sales until its downstream processing facilities achieve normalized operating rates.

PTFI’s consolidated sales volumes of 153 million pounds of copper and 98 thousand ounces of gold in third-quarter 2026 were lower than third-quarter 2025 sales volumes of 360 million pounds of copper and 332 thousand ounces of gold, primarily reflecting lower operating rates at PTFI during the ramp-up of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine. Third-quarter 2026 gold sales volumes were also impacted by the deferral of approximately 60 thousand ounces of refined gold from third-quarter 2026 to fourth-quarter 2026.
In Indonesia, abnormally dry weather conditions have been generally favorable for mining but present various challenges in the milling process. Water availability for the operations and site infrastructure are being actively managed with limited impacts to production to date. Extended periods without precipitation may impact future mill rates and mitigation efforts will continue to be implemented during this period.
PTFI’s unit net cash credits (including by-product credits) of $0.84 per pound of copper in third-quarter 2026 were lower than third-quarter 2025 unit net cash credits of $0.92 per pound of copper, primarily reflecting lower copper and gold volumes.
During the ramp-up period of the Grasberg Block Cave underground mine and until PTFI’s operations return to normal capacity, a portion of PTFI’s production and delivery costs will be recognized as idle facility costs, which are non-inventoriable. Idle facility, direct recovery and restoration costs totaled $244 million ($1.59 per pound of copper) in third-quarter 2026, $934 million ($2.40 per pound of copper) for the first nine months of 2026 and $171 million in both third-quarter 2025 ($0.47 per pound of copper) and for the first nine months of 2025 ($0.16 per pound of copper), which were excluded from PTFI's unit net cash credits.
Consolidated sales volumes from PTFI are expected to approximate 0.7 billion pounds of copper and 632 thousand ounces of gold for the year 2026. Copper and gold production volumes for the year 2026 are expected to exceed sales volumes, reflecting deferrals of approximately 100 million pounds of copper and 70 thousand ounces of gold associated with inventory held at PTFI’s smelting operations.
Based on achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates and assuming an average price of $4,000 per ounce of gold in fourth-quarter 2026, average unit net cash credits (including by-product credits and excluding idle facility and restoration costs) for PTFI are expected to approximate $1.25 per pound of copper for the year 2026. PTFI’s average unit net cash credits for the year 2026 would change by approximately $0.04 per pound of copper for each $100 per ounce change in the average price of gold in fourth-quarter 2026.
Molybdenum Mines. FCX operates two wholly owned primary molybdenum operations in Colorado – the Climax open-pit mine and the Henderson underground mine. The Climax and Henderson mines produce high-purity, chemical-grade molybdenum concentrate, which is typically further processed into value-added molybdenum chemical products. The majority of the molybdenum concentrate produced at the Climax and Henderson mines and at FCX’s U.S. copper mines and Cerro Verde mine is processed at FCX’s conversion facilities.
Operating and Development Activities. Production from the Molybdenum mines totaled 8 million pounds of molybdenum in both the third quarters of 2026 and 2025. FCX’s consolidated molybdenum sales and average realized prices include sales of molybdenum produced at the primary molybdenum operations and at FCX’s U.S. copper mines and Cerro Verde mine, which are presented on page 3.
Average unit net cash costs for the Molybdenum mines of $20.04 per pound of molybdenum in third-quarter 2026 were higher than average unit net cash costs of $19.41 per pound in third-quarter 2025, primarily reflecting higher costs for supplies, labor and energy. Average unit net cash costs for the Molybdenum mines are expected to approximate $18.66 per pound of molybdenum for the year 2026, based on achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates.
For a reconciliation of unit net cash costs per pound to production and delivery costs applicable to sales reported in FCX’s consolidated financial statements, refer to the supplemental schedules, “Product Revenues and Production Costs,” beginning on page XIV.


9
LIQUIDITY, CASH FLOWS, CASH AND DEBT
Liquidity. At September 30, 2026, FCX had $4.3 billion in consolidated cash and cash equivalents. FCX also had $3.0 billion of availability under its revolving credit facility, and PTFI and Cerro Verde had $1.5 billion and $350 million, respectively, of availability under their revolving credit facilities.
Operating Cash Flows. In third-quarter 2026, FCX generated operating cash flows of $2.0 billion, net of $0.4 billion of working capital and other uses, and $5.5 billion, net of $0.8 billion of working capital and other uses, for the first nine months of 2026.
FCX’s consolidated operating cash flows are expected to approximate $8.5 billion for the year 2026, net of $0.6 billion of working capital and other uses, based on current sales volume and cost estimates, and assuming prices of $6.50 per pound of copper, $4,000 per ounce of gold and $32.00 per pound of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026. The impact of price changes during fourth-quarter 2026 on operating cash flows for the year 2026 would approximate $75 million for each $0.10 per pound change in the average price of copper, $25 million for each $100 per ounce change in the average price of gold and $12 million for each $2 per pound change in the average price of molybdenum.
Capital Expenditures. Capital expenditures totaled $1.2 billion in third-quarter 2026, including $0.7 billion for major mining projects, and $3.2 billion for the first nine months of 2026, including $2.0 billion for major mining projects.
Capital expenditures are expected to approximate $4.4 billion for the year 2026, including $3.0 billion for major mining projects. Projected capital expenditures for major mining projects include $1.4 billion for planned projects, primarily associated with underground mine development and supporting mill and power capital costs in the Grasberg minerals district and a leaching project at El Abra, and $1.6 billion for discretionary growth projects.

The terms of the amended facility are substantially similar to PTFI’s prior facility. In addition, FCX’s and Cerro Verde’s revolving credit facilities were extended to 2031 earlier in 2026.

10
At September 30, 2026, there were (i) no borrowings and $5 million in letters of credit issued under FCX’s $3.0 billion revolving credit facility, (ii) $250 million in borrowings outstanding under PTFI’s $1.75 billion revolving credit facility, and (iii) no borrowings outstanding under Cerro Verde’s $350 million revolving credit facility.

FINANCIAL POLICY
FCX’s financial policy is aligned with its strategic objectives of maintaining a solid balance sheet, providing cash returns to common stockholders and advancing opportunities for future growth. The policy includes a base dividend and a performance-based payout framework, whereby up to 50% of available cash flows generated after planned capital spending and distributions to noncontrolling interests would be allocated to common stockholder returns and the balance to debt reduction and investments in value enhancing growth projects, subject to FCX maintaining its net debt at a level not to exceed the net debt target of $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion (excluding project debt for PTFI’s downstream processing facilities). FCX’s Board of Directors (Board) reviews the structure of the performance-based payout framework at least annually.
During the first nine months of 2026, FCX returned $955 million to shareholders, consisting of $650 million in common stock dividends and $305 million in share repurchases.
Net Debt. At September 30, 2026, FCX’s net debt totaled $1.8 billion, which excludes $3.2 billion of debt for PTFI’s downstream processing facilities. Refer to the supplemental schedule, “Net Debt,” on page IX.
Common Stock Dividends. On September 23, 2026, FCX’s Board declared cash dividends totaling $0.15 per share on its common stock (including a $0.075 per share quarterly base cash dividend and a $0.075 per share quarterly variable, performance-based cash dividend), which will be paid on November 2, 2026, to common stockholders of record as of October 15, 2026. The declaration and payment of dividends (base or variable) are at the discretion of the Board and will depend on FCX’s financial results, cash requirements, global economic conditions and other factors deemed relevant by the Board.
Share Repurchase Program. During third-quarter 2026, FCX purchased 1.4 million shares of its common stock for a total cost of $102 million ($70.75 average cost per share), bringing total purchases during the first nine months of 2026 to 4.9 million shares for a total cost of $305 million ($62.69 average cost per share).
At October 26, 2026, FCX has 1.4 billion shares of common stock outstanding and has purchased 56.8 million shares for a total cost of $2.3 billion ($40.58 average cost per share) under its $5.0 billion share repurchase program. The timing and amount of share repurchases is at the discretion of management and will depend on a variety of factors. The share repurchase program may be modified, increased, suspended or terminated at any time at the Board’s discretion.

FREEPORT: Foremost in Copper    
FCX is a leading international metals company with the objective of being foremost in copper. Headquartered in Phoenix, Arizona, FCX operates large, long-lived, geographically diverse assets with significant proven and probable reserves of copper, gold and molybdenum. FCX is one of the world’s largest publicly traded copper producers.
FCX’s portfolio of assets includes the Grasberg minerals district in Indonesia, one of the world’s largest copper and gold deposits; and significant operations in the U.S. and South America, including the large-scale Morenci minerals district in Arizona and the Cerro Verde operation in Peru.

11
By supplying responsibly produced copper, FCX is proud to be a positive contributor to the world well beyond its operational boundaries. Additional information about FCX is available on FCX’s website at fcx.com.

Assuming achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates and prices of $6.50 per pound for copper, $4,000 per ounce for gold and $32.00 per pound for molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026, FCX estimates its consolidated effective tax rate for the year 2026 would approximate 30%, including estimated effective rates of 40% for Peru, 36% for Indonesia and 10% for the U.S. (associated with CAMT provisions). Changes in projected sales volumes, commodity prices, and the relative proportion of jurisdictional income during fourth-quarter 2026 could impact FCX’s consolidated effective tax rate for the year 2026.

NET DEBT
FCX believes that net debt provides investors with information related to the performance-based payout framework in its financial policy, which requires FCX to maintain its net debt at a level not to exceed the net debt target of $3 billion to $4 billion (excluding project debt for PTFI’s downstream processing facilities). FCX defines net debt as consolidated debt less consolidated cash and cash equivalents. This information differs from consolidated debt determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for consolidated debt determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. DERIVATIVE INSTRUMENTS
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, FCX’s mined copper was sold 37% as cathode, 35% as rod, and 28% in concentrate. All of FCX’s copper concentrate and some cathode sales contracts provide final copper pricing in a specified future month (generally one to four months from the shipment date) based primarily on quoted London Metal Exchange (LME) monthly average settlement copper prices. FCX records revenues and invoices customers at the time of shipment based on then-current LME prices, which results in an embedded derivative on provisionally priced concentrate and cathode sales that is adjusted to fair value through earnings each period, using the period-end forward prices, until final pricing on the date of settlement.
FCX’s average realized copper price was $6.54 per pound in third-quarter 2026, reflecting copper sales from South America and Indonesia operations that are generally based on quoted LME monthly average settlement copper prices, which averaged $6.40 per pound in third-quarter 2026, and copper sales from U.S. copper mines that are generally based on prevailing Commodity Exchange Inc. (COMEX) monthly average settlement copper prices, which averaged $6.48 per pound in third-quarter 2026.

At September 30, 2026, FCX had provisionally priced copper sales totaling 239 million pounds (134 million pounds net of intercompany sales and noncontrolling interests) recorded at an average price of $6.55 per pound, subject to final LME settlement prices over the next several months. FCX estimates that each $0.05 change in the price realized from the quarter-end provisional price would have an approximate $12 million effect on 2026 revenues ($4 million to net income attributable to common stock). The LME copper settlement price was $6.58 per pound on October 26, 2026.

DEFERRED PROFITS
FCX defers recognizing profits on intercompany sales from its mining operations to Atlantic Copper until final sales to third parties occur. Changes in these deferrals attributable to variability in intercompany volumes resulted in net additions to operating income totaling $24 million ($8 million to net income attributable to common stock) in third-quarter 2026, $13 million ($15 million to net income attributable to common stock) in third-quarter 2025, $76 million ($25 million to net income attributable to common stock) for the first nine months of 2026 and $161 million ($58 million to net income attributable to common stock) for the first nine months of 2025. FCX’s net deferred profits on inventories at Atlantic Copper to be recognized in future periods’ operating income totaled $77 million ($25 million to net income attributable to common stock) at September 30, 2026. Quarterly variations in ore grades, the timing of intercompany shipments and changes in product prices will result in variability in FCX’s net deferred profits and quarterly earnings.

NONCONTROLLING INTERESTS
Net income attributable to noncontrolling interests, which is primarily associated with PTFI, Cerro Verde and El Abra, totaled $514 million in third-quarter 2026 (which represented 22% of FCX’s consolidated income before income taxes), $573 million in third-quarter 2025 (which represented 30% of FCX’s consolidated income before income taxes), $1.4 billion for the first nine months of 2026 (which represented 23% of FCX’s consolidated income before income taxes) and $1.8 billion for the first nine months of 2025 (which represented 32% of FCX’s consolidated income before income taxes). Refer to “Business Divisions and Segments” below for net income attributable to noncontrolling interests for each of FCX’s business segments.
In May 2026, FCX increased its ownership interest in Cerro Verde from 55.08% to 55.66%.
Based on achievement of current sales volume and cost estimates, and assuming prices of $6.50 per pound of copper, $4,000 per ounce of gold and $32.00 per pound of molybdenum in fourth-quarter 2026, FCX estimates that net income attributable to noncontrolling interests will approximate $2.3 billion for the year 2026, which would represent approximately 24% of FCX’s consolidated income before income taxes. The actual amount will depend on many factors, including relative performance of each business segment, commodity prices, costs and other factors.

BUSINESS DIVISIONS AND SEGMENTS
FCX has organized its mining operations into four primary divisions – U.S. copper mines, South America operations, Indonesia operations and Molybdenum mines.
In the U.S., FCX operates seven copper operations – Morenci, Bagdad, Safford (including Lone Star), Sierrita and Miami in Arizona, and Chino and Tyrone in New Mexico, and two molybdenum mines – Henderson and Climax in Colorado. A majority of the copper produced at the U.S. copper mines is cast into copper rod by the U.S. Rod & Refining operations.
In South America, FCX operates two copper operations – Cerro Verde in Peru and El Abra in Chile.
In Indonesia, PTFI operates the Grasberg minerals district. With the completion of its downstream processing facilities, PTFI is a fully integrated producer of refined copper, gold and silver.
X

FREEPORT
BUSINESS DIVISIONS AND SEGMENTS (continued)
U.S. Rod & Refining consists of copper conversion facilities, including a refinery and two rod mills. These operations process copper produced at FCX’s U.S. copper mines and purchased copper into copper cathode and rod. At times, these operations refine copper and produce copper rod for customers on a toll basis.
Atlantic Copper in Spain smelts and refines copper concentrate and markets refined copper and precious metals in slimes.
Intersegment sales are based on terms similar to arm’s-length transactions with third parties at the time of the sale. Intersegment sales may not be reflective of the actual prices ultimately realized because of a variety of factors, including additional processing, the timing of sales to unaffiliated customers and transportation premiums.
FCX allocates certain operating costs, expenses and capital expenditures to its business divisions and segments. However, not all costs and expenses applicable to an operation are allocated. U.S. federal and state income taxes are recorded and managed at the corporate level (included in Corporate, Other & Eliminations in the below tables), whereas foreign income taxes are recorded and managed at the applicable country level. In addition, some selling, general and administrative costs are not allocated to the business divisions and segments. Accordingly, the following information reflects management determinations that may not be indicative of what the actual financial performance of each business division and segment would be if it was an independent entity.

PRODUCT REVENUES AND PRODUCTION COSTS

FCX believes unit net cash costs (credits) per pound of copper and molybdenum are measures intended to provide investors with information about the cash-generating capacity of its mining operations expressed on a basis relating to the primary metal product for the respective operations. FCX uses this measure for the same purpose and for monitoring operating performance by its mining operations. This information differs from measures of performance determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP and should not be considered in isolation or as a substitute for measures of performance determined in accordance with U.S. GAAP. These measures are presented by other metals mining companies, although FCX’s measures may not be comparable to similarly titled measures reported by other companies.
FCX presents gross profit per pound of copper in the following tables using both a “by-product” method and a “co-product” method. FCX uses the by-product method in its presentation of gross profit per pound of copper because (i) the majority of its revenues are copper revenues, (ii) it mines ore, which contains copper, gold, molybdenum and other metals, (iii) it is not possible to specifically assign all of FCX’s costs to revenues from the copper, gold, molybdenum and other metals it produces and (iv) it is the method used by FCX’s management and Board of Directors to monitor its mining operations and to compare mining operations in certain industry publications. In the co-product method presentations, shared costs are allocated to the different products based on their relative revenue values, which will vary to the extent FCX’s metals sales volumes and realized prices change.
FCX shows revenue adjustments for prior period open sales as a separate line item. Because these adjustments result from prior period sales, these amounts have been reflected separately from revenues on current period sales. Noncash and other costs, net, which are removed from site production and delivery costs in the calculation of unit net cash costs, consist of items such as ARO accretion and other adjustments, inventory write-offs and adjustments, stock-based compensation costs, long-lived asset impairments, idle facility costs, feasibility and optimization study costs, operational readiness and start-up costs, restructuring and/or unusual charges. As discussed above, gold, molybdenum and other metal revenues at copper mines are reflected as credits against site production and delivery costs in the by-product method. The following schedules are presentations under both the by-product and co-product methods together with reconciliations to amounts reported in FCX’s consolidated financial statements.
